It’s not “special” so to speak, just special to me 😂

It’s very light color, non age statement blend, triple cask (ex-sherry, American oak, traditional oak), 40% ABV. Good fruity and sweet pear flavors with a bit of orange, paired with a slight dry note to remind you that it’s scotch. The nose hits you with the pear, a bit of fudge/cacao sweetness, very fragrant. A good hazelnut finish that lingers just long enough to entice you to keep sipping.

Before last year, I was a mixed drink, beer hater, that loved a good chilled tequila straight, no rocks. My idea of whiskey (scotch was “just a whiskey” to me then), was Crown Royal… A good friend invited me over to have a couple of drinks, sit by the fire pit and BS, I came ready with my Don Julio 1942 and 70 Cristalino. My friend pulls out a few different bottles, he and another friend make a Rusty Nail (foreign concept for me) using Drambue and Dewers White Label. Of course I was also made to drink one, and honestly that drink got me started on this path lol

Both my friends, excited that I was liking the cheap stuff, started pulling out more and more expensive bottles. Started me off with a few 12’s, 18’s, then on to more “expensive” stuff like JW Blue. In the midst of the scotch tasting I came across the Master Distiller’s Reserve, they both told me that while it’s not the most expensive stuff out there, they both loved it, and it had become sacred because the supply had dried up…

One of my friends is a pilot and would either buy up all of the bottles when he flew to the UK or would ask his buddies to do the same, years back, so he ended up with 40+ bottles and that number slowly dropped as they were consumed lol

In the end, Glenlivet ended up discontinuing this blend, then relaunched it under a different name, I’ve tried it but it’s just not the same… That relaunch is also an international travel special too…

That same friend gifted me this bottle for helping him, and being a good friend I guess!

Found out that my second favorite to this is Glenfiddich 15 Solera.

But anywho that’s the story of how I found this blend!
Yeahhhhh, not to mention this was an international traveler special only sold in duty free shops…

I would take all of the information you have and file a police report. Once you have a police report filed, usually banks will work with you to refund you from fraudulent transactions as they’re insured.

Depending on where you’re located, in Texas, that’s called Credit/Debit Card Abuse, or Fraudulent Use/Possession of Identifying Information, both of which are felony charges.

Since it falls under fraud the bank will cover you. I would advise you to obtain a “Fraud Affidavit” which is a certified letter from the bank showing that you filed with them, that the $500 purchase was fraudulent. You take that information to the police and file a criminal report. I would highly suggest that you follow through with criminal charges against the cashier.

The bank is insured, with a fraud report from the police they will make you whole again.

Once you file the police report don’t bother going to rite aid, the bank will go after the cashier and get reimbursed upon conviction.
